n: Dr. K.K. Mohammed Koya Sea Cucumber Conservation Reserve
desc: Mohammed Koya Sea Cucumber Conservation Reserve is a marine protected area located off the coast of the Indian union territory of Lakshadweep, approximately 50 km northwest of the island of Bitra. Formally established by Indian authorities on February 27th, 2020, the reserve covers 239 km² of the Arabian Sea, including parts of the Byramgore Reef, and is the world's first conservation area specifically dedicated to the protection of sea cucumbers.

desc: Tungabhadra Otter Conservation Reserve is the first otter conservation reserve in India, located near Hampi in Vijayanagara district in the state of Karnataka. This is a 34 km stretch along Tungabhadra River. The area is well known for smooth-coated otters and soft-shell turtles.

desc: Yangoupokpi-Lokchao Wildlife Sanctuary is an Indo-Burma wildlife sanctuary in Chandel district of Manipur. It is in the Indo-Myanmar border about 110 km from Imphal. It has an area of 184.80 square kilometers.

desc: Kailadevi Wildlife Sanctuary is a protected wildlife area in Karauli district of Rajasthan, India. It was notified in 1983 and covers approximately 676.38 km² area. The sanctuary forms the northern extension of the Ranthambore Tiger Reserve and serves as a wildlife corridor between Ranthambore and the Chambal River region.

desc: Jaisamand Wildlife Sanctuary is a protected area in the Salumbar district of Rajasthan, India, located on the northern and eastern shores of Jaisamand Lake, in aravalli hills about 50 km south of Udaipur. It covers an area of approximately 52.34 km² and is administered by the Rajasthan Forest Department under the Department of Environment, Forests & Climate Change, Government of Rajasthan.

desc: Kalsubai Harishchandragad Wildlife Sanctuary is a protected area located in the northern Western Ghats of Maharashtra, India. Spanning approximately 361.71 km², it is situated primarily within the Akole Tehsil of the Ahmednagar district. The sanctuary houses Mount Kalsubai, the highest peak in Maharashtra, and the historic hill fort of Harishchandragad.

desc: Rakchham Chitkul Wildlife Sanctuary is a protected area located in Sangla valley of the Kinnaur district of Himachal Pradesh, India. It is situated in the arid zone of the middle Himalayas. It covers the area of 304 km².
fact: The sanctuary is home to wildlife, including the Snow Leopard, Himalayan Black Bear, Musk Deer, and Blue Sheep, alongside birds like the Himalayan Monal · The Sanctuary is named after the villages of Rakchham and Chitkul, the latter being the last inhabited village near the Indo-Tibetan border · It is situated in the arid zone of the middle Himalayas

desc: Tokalo Wildlife Sanctuary is a protected area located in the Siaha district of Mizoram, India. Established on October 1, 2007, under the administration of the Mara Autonomous District Council , it spans 250 km² of moist deciduous and semi-evergreen forests. Situated near the Indo-Myanmar border at an altitude of 700 to 940 meters, the sanctuary is a critical biodiversity hotspot.

desc: Jiri-Makru Wildlife Sanctuary is a wildlife sanctuary located in western Manipur, India. It lies between the Jiri and Makru rivers, close to the Assam–Manipur border, and spans parts of Tamenglong district and Jiribam district. The sanctuary contains tropical wet evergreen and semi-evergreen forests and is recognised in conservation listings for its ecological importance.
